greeting.speaker: Bruin the Axe Bear
text: Stand out of the fall line and we'll get on. Everything else about you I can work around.
Wait for the crack, then move. That's the whole of the safety talk and it's saved more men than prayer.
Mind your feet. Half this camp is stump and the other half is what fell on it.

options.text: Why has nothing been cut since spring?
Hand it here. I'll take a turn at the stump.
We're only through for the road.

again.speaker: Bruin the Axe Bear
text: You're back and the road's still crooked. One of those I can do something about.
Sit on the stump. It's the only chair in the valley that's never given anyone a splinter.
Heard you before I saw you. You walk like the ground owes you money.

options.text: Is the cut road any better?
You said you'd swing for us. Still good for it?
Just passing. Keep your line clear.

the_axe.speaker: Bruin the Axe Bear
the_axe.text: A bear with an axe is a woodcutter. A bear without one is a problem. The camp worked that out early and we've all been happier since.

the_stoppage.speaker: Bruin the Axe Bear
the_stoppage.text: Because the cut road goes past a gate, and the gate is open, and the carters have decided timber isn't worth it. They're not wrong.

took_the_stump.speaker: Bruin the Axe Bear
took_the_stump.text: ...Hah. You've done it before. Come back when the road's clear and I'll swing for you instead of at wood.

missed_the_stump.speaker: Bruin the Axe Bear
missed_the_stump.text: You buried it and now you'll get to learn the second half of the job. Pull.

passing.speaker: Bruin the Axe Bear
passing.text: Then go quick and go loud. The quiet ones on that road are the ones we find later.

the_camp.speaker: Bruin the Axe Bear
the_camp.text: Nine, two saws and a cook who can't cook. We were forty. The rest went to look for work, or for the ones who went to look for work.

the_road_now.speaker: Bruin the Axe Bear
text: A cart got through. One. We stood and watched it like it was a parade.
Better where you've been. Worse where you haven't. That's been true all year.
Still bad, but the badness has moved up the valley, and moving is something.

the_offer.speaker: Bruin the Axe Bear
the_offer.text: I'm good for it. Say the word and I'll leave the axe in a stump for the first time in nine years. Just be sure it's a word worth the walk.
